main_topics.reason: The user asked which RA medications are compatible or should be avoided and explored a future medication-switch timeline and alternatives if control worsens.
After saying they had recently started methotrexate, the user asked whether to worry and discussed contraception and stopping it before trying to conceive.
The user asked whether RA may change during pregnancy and engaged with the discussion of possible postpartum flares.
The user asked whether pregnancy-compatible medications are also suitable while breastfeeding.
The user asked whom to coordinate with and whether to raise pregnancy plans with the rheumatologist now, then said they would bring it up at the next visit.
The user described arriving anxious and fearing a choice between their health and having a baby, then said they felt more in control.

output.summary: Recently diagnosed with RA and taking methotrexate, the user wanted to plan medication choices for a pregnancy they hope to try for in one to two years. The assistant discussed medication options and timing, possible changes in RA during pregnancy and postpartum, breastfeeding, and care-team coordination; the user said the discussion eased their anxiety and planned to raise it at their next rheumatology visit.
